newsitem.title: CANADA: Thailand says near trade deal with Taiwan-RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says near trade deal with Taiwan-RFTV.

text.p: Thailand is inching closer to a bilateral trade deal with Taiwan, and prospects for Taiwan's admission to the World Trade Organization (WTO) are good, Thai Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasonee said at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
If Taiwan opened certain sectors of the economy to Thai products, Thailand was ready to "sign on the dotted line," Akrasonee told Reuters financial television in an interview broadcast on Friday.
Akrasonee added that Thailand was also working on a similar trade deal with China and denied that the talks with Taiwan had caused any friction with officials in Beijing.
"It's only trade," Akrasonee said. "We have been positive to both of them (joining the WTO) because we are very objective about it. There is no politics in it."
Thailand is pursuing an aggressive campaign to lower tariff barriers in Asia in an attempt to bolster the sluggish Thai economy.
Analysts said the country faced a bearish economic outlook and the Thai currency, the baht, was susceptible to speculative market attacks.

Akrasonee said Thai officials were working to restore investor confidence and that the economy would grow at 10 percent in 1997, much of it on the basis of an expected surge in exports to Hong Kong, China and Taiwan.
"Exports to Southeast Asian countries are growing very fast. Combined they are the biggest market for us now," Akrasonee said.
